title: vendor-service BYPASS_PERMISSIONS must never regress to an unconditional true
description: Historical defect (RBAC-003 / BAC-003, tracked in QA_Tracker/RBAC/BROKEN_ACCESS_CONTROL_FINDINGS.md): keycloak.ts previously had `const BYPASS_PERMISSIONS = true;` hardcoded, disabling all vendor-service RBAC. The current code (keycloak.ts:140) gates it as `NODE_ENV !== 'production' && BYPASS_PERMISSIONS === 'true'` plus an explicit startup guard (line 223-224) that throws if this is ever true in production. This case guards against reverting either safeguard.
steps: Start the service with NODE_ENV=production, BYPASS_PERMISSIONS=true
expectedResult: The definition remains env-gated (never a bare `= true`), and startup throws 'BYPASS_PERMISSIONS must not be true in production' rather than serving traffic with RBAC disabled.

title: CUSTOMER_BASELINE_PERMISSIONS must remain empty for direct_customer and mssp_client organizations
description: Historical defect (RBAC-022): project.read, user.read, dashboard.read were unconditionally injected into every user's permission set regardless of role, effectively bypassing role restrictions for those three module reads. loadPermissions.js:44 now sets CUSTOMER_BASELINE_PERMISSIONS = [] by deliberate design (2026-07-19) — those routes now self-scope via membership/shared-project logic instead of a blanket permission grant. This case guards against silently reintroducing entries into that array.
steps: As a NORMAL_USER with zero project memberships, call GET /api/client/users/me and inspect the permissions array
expectedResult: CUSTOMER_BASELINE_PERMISSIONS is still []. The returned permissions array for this user contains none of project.read/user.read/dashboard.read as a blanket grant.

title: auth.controller.js must keep routing through verifyKeycloakToken(), never jwt.decode(), for authorization decisions
description: Historical defects BAC-001 (admin/authorize using jwt.decode()) and BAC-002 (OAuth callback's decodePayload() using jwt.decode()). Current auth.controller.js's decodePayload() (line 96-99) calls verifyKeycloakToken(), which performs full RS256/JWKS signature verification. This case guards against either endpoint regressing to a raw, unverified decode.
steps: grep auth.controller.js for any direct `jwt.decode(` call used to derive claims that feed an authorization decision
Submit a JWT with a forged resource_access.admin-portal claim and an invalid/missing signature to POST /api/auth/admin/authorize
expectedResult: No authorization-relevant code path calls jwt.decode() directly — only verifyKeycloakToken()/jwt.verify() with algorithms:['RS256']. The forged-signature request is rejected, not granted admin access.

title: DEV_BYPASS must remain an allow-list (NODE_ENV==='development'), never a deny-list (NODE_ENV!=='production')
description: authenticate.js:24-28 documents the historical risk explicitly: a deny-list (`!== 'production'`) would leave DEV_BYPASS reachable in any unlabeled/staging environment. The current allow-list requires NODE_ENV to be exactly 'development' AND DEV_BYPASS==='true'. This case guards against the comparison being loosened back to a deny-list during a future refactor.
steps: Set NODE_ENV='staging', DEV_BYPASS='true'; send a request with no Authorization header
expectedResult: The definition still reads `... && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` (not `!== 'production'`). With NODE_ENV='staging', the request is NOT auto-authenticated as the dev fixture user — it proceeds to require a real Bearer token and is rejected with 401.

title: trust-vault-service's internal-token comparison must remain constant-time
description: Historical defect class RBAC-016 (timing oracle on a DEV_BYPASS token comparison in vciso-service, via naive === string comparison). trust-vault-service/src/routes/s2s.routes.ts:63-73 now uses crypto.timingSafeEqual with an explicit equal-length guard. This case guards against the comparison regressing to a plain `===` or `provided === expectedToken` check anywhere in the S2S auth path.
steps: Inspect validateInternalToken() in s2s.routes.ts for any direct string equality comparison of the internal token
Statistically measure response latency for near-correct vs. wildly-incorrect token guesses across many requests
expectedResult: Only timingSafeEqual (with the length-guard pattern) is used for the comparison. Latency does not measurably correlate with how many leading characters of the guess were correct.

title: 'project.admin' must remain excluded from ORG_ONLY_MODULE_PERMISSIONS and rejected by assertNoOrgWideProjectBypass
description: Fixed 2026-07-22 (SEC-3, per config/permissions.js's own comment): 'project.admin' — the org-wide project-membership bypass — was previously assignable through the Extra Permissions modal / a Custom Role grid. It is now deliberately excluded from the org-grantable catalog and independently rejected by catalogSeparation.js's assertNoOrgWideProjectBypass on every Role/User write. This case guards against either safeguard being removed.
steps: Call GET /master/enums (the Extra Permissions modal's data source) and confirm 'project.admin' is not listed as a grantable org-wide permission
Attempt to submit 'project.admin' via POST /api/roles or PUT /api/users/:id/extra-permissions
expectedResult: 'project.admin' never appears in the enumerable grant catalog surfaced to the UI, and any direct API attempt to assign it to a Custom Role or a User's extraPermissions is rejected with 400.
